findings.summary: Active-set rollback can republish a package whose provenance is revoked by the current trust policy.
findings.evidence: The rollback branch at extension_activation.py:1466-1476 compares the current revocation set only with the target activation record, package identity, and manifest. It loads the ingest record afterward but never compares the ingest, source-attestation, build-attestation, publisher-signature, or production-policy digests used by the initial activation gate at lines 1197-1214. In an independently executed disposable-repository mutation, current policy generation 2 revoked source-attestation sha256-jcs-v1:720cd3db594411757803b2b59ad3d499486ff1c1cfbff2fcb9189377c362d84a; rollback still returned ALLOWED, published generation 3, and selected v1 activation sha256-jcs-v1:1c8bafdb443df8273a8cdf9d2159dfede252fd057514b1ec464255e13a94e7be. ADR-0004 line 838 requires rollback to select only a complete old extension set that still satisfies current trust, revocation, and compatibility.
findings.required_change: Before any rollback data-registry, activation-manifest, or pointer write, re-evaluate the target package against the current trust tuple using one shared fail-closed eligibility path. At minimum bind and check the exact activation, ingest, package identity, manifest, source attestation, build attestation, publisher signature, and production-policy subjects; current installed production-policy/key/source/namespace/kind/capability/compatibility/resource rules; the data-only and non-built-in-executable gates; and immutable installed-content doctor results. Return a stable non-disclosing denial with zero active-set mutation when any current requirement fails.
findings.verification: Add a production-path rollback matrix that first supersedes v1 with v2, then independently revokes each v1 subject (activation, ingest, package identity, manifest, source attestation, build attestation, publisher signature, and production policy) and proves every rollback is denied before registry/manifest/pointer writes. Add current-policy tightening cases for relevant key, production policy, source, namespace, kind, capability ceiling, compatibility floor, and resource binding; each must deny rollback, while unrelated expansion and an unchanged fully eligible v1 preserve the valid rollback path. Assert restart observes the exact pre-request generation after every denial.
mechanical_closure_tests: Supersede v1 with v2, commit a current source-attestation revocation for v1, request rollback to v1, and assert E_EXTENSION_REVOKED plus byte-identical active pointer, manifest, data registry, and activation ledger.
Repeat for activation record, ingest record, package identity, manifest, build attestation, publisher signature, and production policy; no subject class may be omitted from the shared rollback check.

Tighten each relevant current trust and compatibility dimension after v1 activation and prove rollback rejects before publication; retain positive rollback for an unchanged eligible package and for irrelevant authority contraction/expansion cases defined by policy.
Restart after every rejected rollback and prove the prior active generation and revocation high-water remain authoritative with no orphan registry or manifest row.
